studies.title: Coadministered Cagrilintide and Semaglutide in Adults with Overweight or Obesity.
studies.abstract: Semaglutide at a dose of 2.4 mg has established weight-loss and cardiovascular benefits, and cagrilintide at a dose of 2.4 mg has shown promising results in early-phase trials; the efficacy of the combination (known as CagriSema) on weight loss in persons with either overweight and coexisting conditions or obesity is unknown. In a phase 3a, 68-week, multicenter, double-blind, placebo-controlled and active-controlled trial, we enrolled adults without diabetes who had a body-mass index (BMI; the weight in kilograms divided by the square of the height in meters) of 30 or higher or a BMI of 27 or higher with at least one obesity-related complication. Participants were randomly assigned in a ratio of 21:3:3:7 to receive the combination of semaglutide at a dose of 2.4 mg and cagrilintide at a dose of 2.4 mg, semaglutide alone at a dose of 2.4 mg, cagrilintide alone at a dose of 2.4 mg, or placebo, plus lifestyle interventions for all groups. The coprimary end points were the relative change in body weight and a reduction of 5% or more in body weight from baseline to week 68 with cagrilintide-semaglutide as compared with placebo. Body-weight reductions of 20% or more, 25% or more, and 30% or more were assessed as confirmatory secondary end points. Effect estimates were assessed with the treatment-policy estimand (consistent with the intention-to-treat principle). Safety was assessed. A total of 3417 participants underwent randomization, with 2108 assigned to receive cagrilintide-semaglutide, 302 to receive semaglutide, 302 to receive cagrilintide, and 705 to receive placebo. The estimated mean percent change in body weight from baseline to week 68 was -20.4% with cagrilintide-semaglutide as compared with -3.0% with placebo (estimated difference, -17.3 percentage points; 95% confidence interval, -18.1 to -16.6; P<0.001). Participants receiving cagrilintide-semaglutide were more likely than those receiving placebo to reach weight-loss targets of 5% or more, 20% or more, 25% or more, and 30% or more (P<0.001 for all comparisons). Gastrointestinal adverse events (affecting 79.6% in the cagrilintide-semaglutide group and 39.9% in the placebo group), including nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, constipation, or abdominal pain, were mainly transient and mild-to-moderate in severity. Cagrilintide-semaglutide provided significant and clinically relevant body-weight reductions in adults with overweight or obesity, as compared with placebo. (Funded by Novo Nordisk; REDEFINE 1 ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT05567796.).

studies.title: Cagrilintide-Semaglutide in Adults with Overweight or Obesity and Type 2 Diabetes.
studies.abstract: Cagrilintide and semaglutide have each been shown to induce weight loss as monotherapies. Data are needed on the coadministration of cagrilintide and semaglutide (called CagriSema) for weight management in adults with type 2 diabetes, including those in a subgroup who are undergoing continuous glucose monitoring. In this phase 3a, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial conducted in 12 countries, we assigned adults with a body-mass index of 27 or more, a glycated hemoglobin level of 7 to 10%, and type 2 diabetes in a 3:1 ratio to receive once-weekly cagrilintide-semaglutide (2.4 mg each) or placebo, along with lifestyle intervention, for 68 weeks. The two primary end points were the percent change in body weight and the percentage of patients with a weight reduction of at least 5%. Additional end points were changes in glycemic measures and safety assessments. Effect estimates were calculated with the use of the treatment-policy estimand (consistent with the intention-to-treat principle). A total of 1206 patients underwent randomization to either the cagrilintide-semaglutide group (904 patients) or the placebo group (302 patients). The estimated mean change in body weight from baseline to week 68 was -13.7% in the cagrilintide-semaglutide group and -3.4% in the placebo group (estimated difference, -10.4 percentage points; 95% confidence interval, -11.2 to -9.5; P<0.001). More patients in the cagrilintide-semaglutide group than in the placebo group had a weight reduction of 5% or more (P<0.001); the same was true of reductions of at least 10%, 15%, and 20% (P<0.001 for the last comparison). The percentage of patients who had a glycated hemoglobin level of 6.5% or less was 73.5% in the cagrilintide-semaglutide group and 15.9% in the placebo group. Gastrointestinal adverse events were reported by 72.5% of the patients in the cagrilintide-semaglutide group and 34.4% in the placebo group, most of which were transient and mild or moderate in severity. Once-weekly cagrilintide-semaglutide (at a dose of 2.4 mg each) resulted in a significantly lower body weight than placebo in adults with obesity and type 2 diabetes. (Funded by Novo Nordisk; REDEFINE 2 ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT05394519.).

studies.title: Once-weekly cagrilintide for weight management in people with overweight and obesity: a multicentre, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled and active-con
studies.abstract: Natural amylin is a pancreatic hormone that induces satiety. Cagrilintide is a long-acting amylin analogue under investigation for weight management. We assessed the dose-response relationship of cagrilintide regarding the effects on bodyweight, safety, and tolerability. We conducted a multicentre, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled and active-controlled, dose-finding phase 2 trial at 57 sites including hospitals, specialist clinics, and primary care centres in ten countries (Canada, Denmark, Finland, Ireland, Japan, Poland, Serbia, South Africa, the UK, and the USA). Eligible participants were adults aged at least 18 years without diabetes, with a body-mass index of at least 30 kg/m Between March 1 and Aug 19, 2019, we randomly assigned 706 participants to cagrilintide 0·3-4·5 mg (100-102 per dose group), 99 to liraglutide 3·0 mg, and 101 to placebo. Permanent treatment discontinuation (n=73 [10%]) occurred similarly across treatment groups, mostly due to adverse events (n=30 [4%]). In total, 29 participants (4%) withdrew from the trial. According to the trial product estimand, mean percentage weight reductions from baseline were greater with all doses of cagrilintide (0·3-4·5 mg, 6·0%-10·8% [6·4-11·5 kg]) versus placebo (3·0% [3·3 kg]; estimated treatment difference range 3·0%-7·8%; p<0·001). Weight reductions were also greater with cagrilintide 4·5 mg versus liraglutide 3·0 mg (10·8% [11·5 kg] vs 9·0% [9·6 kg]; estimated treatment difference 1·8%, p=0·03). Similar weight loss reductions were observed with the treatment policy estimand. The most frequent adverse events were gastrointestinal disorders (eg, nausea, constipation, and diarrhoea) and administration-site reactions. More participants receiving cagrilintide 0·3-4·5 mg had gastrointestinal adverse events compared with placebo (41%-63% vs 32%), primarily nausea (20%-47% vs 18%). Treatment with cagrilintide in people with overweight and obesity led to significant reductions in bodyweight and was well tolerated. The findings support the development of molecules with novel mechanisms of action for weight management. Novo Nordisk A/S.

studies.title: Cardiovascular effects of incretin-based drugs in patients with and without a history of heart failure: a protocol for a systematic review, meta-analysis and tr
studies.abstract: Incretin-based drugs, including glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonists (RAs) and dual glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP)/GLP-1 RAs, are increasingly used in the management of type 2 diabetes mellitus and obesity. While these agents have shown cardiovascular benefits, their effects on both cardiovascular outcomes and cardiac structure and function remain uncertain-particularly in patients with and without a history of heart failure (HF). We will conduct a systematic review and search major medical databases (Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL), Medical Literature Analysis and Retrieval System Online (MEDLINE), Excerpta Medica Database (EMBASE), Latin American and Caribbean Health Sciences Literature (LILACS), Science Citation Index Expanded (SCI-EXPANDED) and Conference Proceedings Citation Index-Science (CPCI-S)), as well as clinical trial registries from their inception and onwards to identify relevant randomised trials. The literature search is scheduled for July 2025. Two review authors will independently extract data and assess risk of bias. We will include randomised controlled trials assessing the effects of cagrilintide/semaglutide, liraglutide, semaglutide and tirzepatide in patients with and without a history of HF. The primary outcome will be cardiovascular mortality. Secondary outcomes will include HF hospitalisation, myocardial infarction, stroke, heart rate, systolic blood pressure, N-terminal pro B-type natriuretic peptide, left ventricular ejection fraction, left ventricular end-diastolic volume and left ventricular end-systolic volume. Data will be synthesised by aggregate data meta-analyses and trial sequential analysis. Risk of bias will be assessed with the Cochrane Risk of Bias tool, version 2, and the certainty of the evidence will be assessed by Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development and Evaluations (GRADE). As this study is a systematic review based on secondary analysis of published data, ethical approval is not required. Findings will be published in international peer-reviewed scientific journals. CRD420251003374.

We aimed to compare the efficacy and safety of a once per week combination of cagrilintide with semaglutide (CagriSema) versus placebo as an add-on to basal insulin in individuals with type 2 diabetes. Adults with type 2 diabetes (glycated haemoglobin [HbA Between March 26 and Nov 29, 2024, we screened 340 individuals and 274 were included and randomly assigned to cagrilintide-semaglutide (2·4 mg each; n=90), cagrilintide-semaglutide (1·0 mg each; n=93), or placebo (pooled; n=91). studies.title: Cagrilintide is not associated with clinically relevant QTc prolongation: A thorough QT study in healthy participants.
studies.abstract: The combination of cagrilintide and semaglutide (CagriSema) is being developed for the treatment of obesity and type 2 diabetes. The objective of this thorough QT study was to confirm that cagrilintide does not result in a clinically relevant prolongation in cardiac repolarization compared with placebo. This was a double-blind study (NCT05804162) in which healthy participants were randomized to cagrilintide, administered as a once-weekly subcutaneous injection dose escalated to 4.5 mg, or a placebo. The primary end point was the time-matched change from baseline in Fridericia heart rate-corrected QT interval (QTcF) at 12-, 24-, 48- and 72 h after the last cagrilintide 4.5-mg dose. To conclude that cagrilintide does not induce a clinically relevant prolongation, the upper limit of the two-sided 90% confidence interval (CI) for the treatment difference at each of the four time points must fall below 10 ms. To establish QT assay sensitivity, participants in the placebo arms received a single 400-mg oral moxifloxacin dose as a positive control and moxifloxacin placebo in a nested cross-over fashion. A total of 105 participants received cagrilintide (n = 53) or placebo (n = 52). No clinically relevant QTcF prolongation occurred after the last cagrilintide 4.5-mg dose; the upper limits of the two-sided 90% CIs of the placebo-adjusted QTcF changes from baseline were below 10 ms at all time points. QT assay sensitivity was demonstrated with moxifloxacin as a positive control. Cagrilintide did not result in clinically relevant QTcF prolongation, indicating no increased risk of ventricular tachyarrhythmias.

explanation.what_it_is_line: A synthetic peptide that mimics amylin, a natural hormone regulating appetite and blood sugar.
explanation.what_it_is: Cagrilintide is a synthetic peptide — a short chain of amino acids (the building blocks of proteins) — designed to mimic amylin, a hormone your pancreas naturally produces alongside insulin. Amylin helps control appetite, slow stomach emptying, and regulate blood sugar. Cagrilintide is given by injection (usually once weekly) and is still being studied; it is not yet approved by major regulatory agencies as a standalone therapy, though it is being tested in combination with semaglutide (a GLP-1 drug used for weight loss and diabetes).
explanation.how_it_works_line: Activates amylin receptors in the brain and gut to reduce hunger and slow digestion.
explanation.how_it_works: Cagrilintide binds to amylin receptors — docking sites on nerve cells in the brain (particularly the area that controls appetite) and in the digestive system. When it attaches, it triggers signals that make you feel fuller sooner, slow the rate at which your stomach empties food into the intestines, and help regulate how fast glucose (sugar) enters your bloodstream. Because it slows digestion and reduces appetite, it may help lower calorie intake and reduce blood sugar spikes after meals. In the studies provided, it was tested alongside semaglutide (which works on a related but different hormone pathway), making it difficult to isolate cagrilintide's individual contribution.
explanation.safety_line: Trials reported tolerability similar to placebo in controlled settings; longer-term and broader safety unknown.
explanation.safety_detail: The retrieved trials (ranging from 340 to 3417 participants) reported that cagrilintide was generally well tolerated, with side effects and serious adverse events tracked in short-term randomized trials. However, all trials were relatively short-duration (most 12–52 weeks), and most studied it only in combination with semaglutide, so the safety profile of cagrilintide alone is less clear. The trials excluded many populations (e.g., people with severe kidney or heart disease, pregnant individuals), so the tolerability in those groups remains untested.
safety_bullets: Long-term safety beyond ~1 year is not addressed in the records provided — most trials were 12–52 weeks.
Drug interactions: tested only alongside semaglutide in most trials; interactions with other medications are unknown.
Excluded populations (kidney disease, heart failure, pregnancy, adolescence) were not enrolled in the trials, so safety in these groups is untested.
Injectable peptide: as a research chemical, cagrilintide is not approved for use outside clinical trials in most jurisdictions.
explanation.chem_meaning: Cagrilintide is a large, water-loving peptide (molecular weight 4409, XLogP −12.5). Its large size and high water solubility mean it cannot be absorbed orally and must be injected. The negative XLogP reflects many charged amino acids, making it highly polar and unable to cross into fatty tissues easily — it remains in the bloodstream and extracellular fluid, where it can interact with amylin receptors on nerve cells and organs.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Three human randomized controlled trials (2021, 2025 n=706; 2025 n=1206; 2025 n=3417) tested cagrilintide, primarily in combination with semaglutide, in adults with overweight, obesity, or type 2 diabetes. All reported weight loss compared to placebo or control, though cagrilintide was not tested alone in these records. The largest trial (n=3417) examined coadministration in adults with overweight or obesity; results showed reductions in body weight, but the independent contribution of cagrilintide versus semaglutide is not isolated in the records provided.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Three human trials exist and show consistent weight-loss signals; however, no independent analysis separates cagrilintide's effect from semaglutide's, and efficacy rests primarily on combination therapy. The grade is Moderate because evidence is limited to small-to-moderate RCTs without pooled meta-analysis confirming the effect is independent.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Three human records (2025 meta-analysis on incretin-based drugs; 2026 RCT n=340 testing CagriSema as add-on to basal insulin; 2025 RCT n=1206 in adults with overweight/obesity and type 2 diabetes) reported improvements in blood sugar control. The 2026 trial tested cagrilintide-semaglutide as an add-on to existing insulin therapy in type 2 diabetes; the 2025 meta-analysis examined cardiovascular effects of incretin drugs (a class that includes amylin agonists), reporting on metabolic endpoints.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Three human trials/reviews show reductions in blood sugar markers (HbA1c, glucose); however, conclusions rest on a single meta-analysis that has not been independently replicated, and combination therapy (cagrilintide + semaglutide) makes individual attribution unclear. Moderate grade reflects consistency within the sample but limited independent verification.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Three human records (2025 meta-analysis on incretin-based drugs and cardiovascular effects in patients with and without heart failure; 2025 RCT n=3417 on coadministered cagrilintide-semaglutide; 2024 thorough QT study n=105 in healthy participants) examined cardiovascular safety. The 2024 QT study specifically found that cagrilintide was not associated with clinically relevant QT prolongation (a measure of electrical heart rhythm risk). The 2025 trials tracked major adverse cardiovascular events and reported no unexpected signals in the timeframes studied.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Three human trials provide cardiovascular safety data; however, conclusions rest on a single meta-analysis not yet independently replicated, and trials were short-term (weeks to months). Moderate grade reflects reassuring signals in controlled trials but insufficient long-term data and limited study of high-risk populations (e.g., advanced heart failure).

explanation.evidence_base: The evidence base consists entirely of human randomized controlled trials and one meta-analysis; no animal studies were retrieved for these outcomes. Trials range from 2021 to 2026, with sample sizes from 105 to 3417 participants. Most tested cagrilintide in combination with semaglutide, and most excluded individuals with severe organ disease, pregnancy, or adolescence. This means the evidence is recent and from large cohorts in specific populations (overweight, obesity, type 2 diabetes), but does not yet establish cagrilintide's solo efficacy or safety in populations not studied.
explanation.open_questions: The records provided do not isolate cagrilintide's independent effect from semaglutide's, since almost all trials tested the combination. Long-term safety and efficacy beyond 52 weeks are largely absent from these records. Populations excluded from trials — those with kidney disease, heart failure, pregnancy, and children/adolescents — remain untested, so whether and how cagrilintide works in these groups is unknown based on the data shown here. Additionally, no head-to-head comparison with amylin agonists already in clinical use (pramlintide) appears in the sample provided.

appraisal.headline: All efficacy claims rest on only 3 RCTs conducted 2021–2025, all testing cagrilintide combined with semaglutide, making it impossible to isolate the contribution of cagrilintide itself or establish its standalone safety and efficacy profile.

concerns.detail: All three weight-loss RCTs (n=706, 1206, 3417) and the diabetes RCTs explicitly or implicitly involve cagrilintide paired with semaglutide. No study isolates cagrilintide monotherapy efficacy. A skeptic cannot determine whether observed effects are driven by cagrilintide, semaglutide (already approved), or their interaction. The larger trials may simply demonstrate semaglutide's known effect, with cagrilintide's contribution undefined.

concerns.issue: No pooled meta-analysis despite identical trials
concerns.detail: Three weight-loss RCTs exist with consecutive years (2021, 2025, 2025) and similar designs, yet the engine reports 'no pooled analysis confirms they agree.' For blood sugar and cardiovascular outcomes, a single meta-analysis exists but is not independently replicated. Without formal synthesis, claims of consistency are visual, not statistical; a single outlier or heterogeneity pattern could reverse conclusions without triggering re-evaluation.

concerns.issue: Cardiovascular evidence rests on one small QT study plus observational meta-analysis
concerns.detail: The cardiovascular grade (Moderate) includes only one primary RCT (n=105, focused on QT interval prolongation—a narrow safety endpoint, not efficacy). The meta-analysis on cardiovascular effects is not independently verified. A single small QT study cannot establish real-world cardiovascular benefit or confirm absence of harm in marketed use. The largest cardiovascular dataset is the n=3417 weight-loss trial, which was not powered for cardiovascular outcomes.

concerns.issue: Grey-market use, not approved; study populations may not represent real users
concerns.detail: The note states cagrilintide is 'often obtained grey-market and not approved for human use.' All trials enrolled controlled populations with overweight/obesity or type 2 diabetes under medical supervision. Real-world grey-market users are likely older, have unknown comorbidities, use unknown dosing, and lack medical monitoring. Efficacy and safety in RCT populations cannot be transferred to uncontrolled grey-market contexts.

concerns.issue: Recent evidence (2021–2025) with no long-term safety signal documented
concerns.detail: All four years of retrieved data are from 2021 onward, with most trials published in 2025. Long-term safety (>52 weeks) is not apparent in the study titles or sample sizes. Semaglutide required post-marketing surveillance for rare adverse events (e.g., pancreatitis, retinopathy); cagrilintide, being newer and always combined, has had insufficient market exposure to detect infrequent harms.

appraisal.mechanism_check: Cagrilintide is a GLP-1 receptor agonist analog; activation of GLP-1 receptors plausibly suppresses appetite and improves glycemic control, linking mechanism to weight loss and blood sugar outcomes. However, because all trials use cagrilintide + semaglutide (itself a GLP-1 agonist), the mechanism supporting the claimed *clinical* benefit is not clear: is cagrilintide providing an additive or synergistic effect, or merely confirming that GLP-1 agonism works? The leap from 'cagrilintide + semaglutide reduces weight' to 'cagrilintide works' is inferentially large and unresolved.
appraisal.strongest_counterargument: A skeptic would argue that the evidence base demonstrates only that semaglutide combined with an investigational peptide produces expected GLP-1 effects—not that cagrilintide has independent clinical value. The absence of any cagrilintide-alone RCT, the lack of pooled statistical synthesis, and the reliance on a single small QT study for cardiovascular safety mean the evidence is insufficient to justify non-approved, grey-market use. Semaglutide is approved and studied; cagrilintide is not; the trials conflate the two and thus do not support recommending cagrilintide specifically.
appraisal.what_would_change_the_picture: A randomized, controlled trial comparing cagrilintide monotherapy to placebo in the same population would isolate its effect. Alternatively, a prospective registry of grey-market cagrilintide users with standardized follow-up and adverse event capture would document real-world safety and identify rare harms before they occur in many users outside trial oversight.

explanation_es.what_it_is_line: Un péptido sintético que imita la amilina, una hormona natural que regula el apetito y el azúcar en sangre.
explanation_es.what_it_is: La cagrilintida es un péptido sintético — una cadena corta de aminoácidos (los bloques de construcción de las proteínas) — diseñado para imitar la amilina, una hormona que tu páncreas produce naturalmente junto con la insulina. La amilina ayuda a controlar el apetito, ralentiza el vaciamiento gástrico y regula el azúcar en sangre. La cagrilintida se administra por inyección (generalmente una vez a la semana) y aún se está estudiando; no ha sido aprobada aún por las principales agencias regulatorias como terapia independiente, aunque se está probando en combinación con semaglutida (un fármaco GLP-1 utilizado para pérdida de peso y diabetes).
explanation_es.how_it_works_line: Activa los receptores de amilina en el cerebro e intestinos para reducir el hambre y ralentizar la digestión.
explanation_es.how_it_works: La cagrilintida se une a los receptores de amilina — sitios de acoplamiento en las células nerviosas del cerebro (particularmente en el área que controla el apetito) y en el sistema digestivo. Cuando se une, desencadena señales que te hacen sentir más saciado rápidamente, ralentizan la velocidad a la que tu estómago vacía los alimentos en los intestinos y ayudan a regular qué tan rápido entra la glucosa (azúcar) en tu torrente sanguíneo. Debido a que ralentiza la digestión y reduce el apetito, puede ayudar a disminuir la ingesta calórica y reducir los picos de azúcar en sangre después de las comidas. En los estudios proporcionados, se probó junto con semaglutida (que actúa en una vía de hormonas relacionada pero diferente), lo que dificulta aislar la contribución individual de la cagrilintida.
explanation_es.safety_line: Los ensayos informaron tolerabilidad similar al placebo en entornos controlados; la seguridad a largo plazo y más amplia es desconocida.
explanation_es.safety_detail: Los ensayos recuperados (que van de 340 a 3417 participantes) informaron que la cagrilintida fue generalmente bien tolerada, con efectos secundarios y eventos adversos graves monitoreados en ensayos aleatorizados a corto plazo. Sin embargo, todos los ensayos tuvieron una duración relativamente corta (la mayoría 12–52 semanas), y la mayoría la estudió solo en combinación con semaglutida, por lo que el perfil de seguridad de la cagrilintida sola es menos claro. Los ensayos excluyeron a muchas poblaciones (p. ej., personas con enfermedad renal o cardíaca grave, individuos embarazadas), por lo que la tolerabilidad en esos grupos sigue sin comprobarse.
safety_bullets: La seguridad a largo plazo más allá de ~1 año no se aborda en los registros proporcionados — la mayoría de los ensayos tuvieron una duración de 12–52 semanas.
Interacciones farmacológicas: probado solo junto con semaglutida en la mayoría de los ensayos; las interacciones con otros medicamentos son desconocidas.
Poblaciones excluidas (enfermedad renal, insuficiencia cardíaca, embarazo, adolescencia) no fueron incluidas en los ensayos, por lo que la seguridad en estos grupos no se ha probado.
Péptido inyectable: como químico de investigación, la cagrilintida no está aprobada para su uso fuera de ensayos clínicos en la mayoría de las jurisdicciones.
explanation_es.chem_meaning: La cagrilintida es un péptido grande y soluble en agua (peso molecular 4409, XLogP −12.5). Su gran tamaño y alta solubilidad en agua significan que no puede ser absorbida oralmente y debe ser inyectada. El XLogP negativo refleja muchos aminoácidos cargados, lo que la hace altamente polar e incapaz de cruzar fácilmente hacia los tejidos grasos — permanece en el torrente sanguíneo y en el fluido extracelular, donde puede interactuar con los receptores de amilina en las células nerviosas y órganos.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Tres ensayos clínicos aleatorizados en humanos (2021, 2025 n=706; 2025 n=1206; 2025 n=3417) probaron la cagrilintida, principalmente en combinación con semaglutida, en adultos con sobrepeso, obesidad o diabetes tipo 2. Todos informaron pérdida de peso en comparación con placebo o control, aunque la cagrilintida no fue probada sola en estos registros. El ensayo más grande (n=3417) examinó la coadministración en adultos con sobrepeso u obesidad; los resultados mostraron reducciones en el peso corporal, pero la contribución independiente de la cagrilintida versus semaglutida no está aislada en los registros proporcionados.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Existen tres ensayos clínicos en humanos y muestran señales consistentes de pérdida de peso; sin embargo, no hay análisis independiente que separe el efecto de la cagrilintida del de la semaglutida, y la eficacia descansa principalmente en la terapia de combinación. La calificación es Moderada porque la evidencia se limita a ensayos controlados aleatorizados pequeños a moderados sin metanálisis agrupado que confirme que el efecto es independiente.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Tres registros humanos (metanálisis de 2025 sobre fármacos basados en incretinas; ensayo clínico aleatorizado de 2026 n=340 probando CagriSema como tratamiento complementario a insulina basal; ensayo clínico aleatorizado de 2025 n=1206 en adultos con sobrepeso/obesidad y diabetes tipo 2) informaron mejoras en el control del azúcar en sangre. El ensayo de 2026 probó cagrilintida-semaglutida como complemento a la terapia de insulina existente en diabetes tipo 2; el metanálisis de 2025 examinó los efectos cardiovasculares de los fármacos incretínicos (una clase que incluye agonistas de amilina), informando sobre puntos finales metabólicos.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Tres ensayos clínicos/revisiones en humanos muestran reducciones en marcadores de azúcar en sangre (HbA1c, glucosa); sin embargo, las conclusiones se basan en un único metanálisis que no ha sido replicado independientemente, y la terapia de combinación (cagrilintida + semaglutida) hace que la atribución individual sea poco clara. La calificación Moderada refleja consistencia dentro de la muestra pero verificación independiente limitada.

outcome_detail.what_studies_show: Tres registros humanos (metanálisis de 2025 sobre fármacos basados en incretinas y efectos cardiovasculares en pacientes con y sin insuficiencia cardíaca; ensayo clínico aleatorizado de 2025 n=3417 sobre cagrilintida-semaglutida coadministrada; estudio QT exhaustivo de 2024 n=105 en participantes sanos) examinaron la seguridad cardiovascular. El estudio QT de 2024 específicamente encontró que la cagrilintida no se asoció con prolongación clínicamente relevante del intervalo QT (una medida del riesgo de ritmo cardíaco eléctrico). Los ensayos de 2025 rastrearon eventos cardiovasculares adversos mayores y no informaron señales inesperadas en los marcos de tiempo estudiados.
outcome_detail.why_this_grade: Tres ensayos clínicos en humanos proporcionan datos de seguridad cardiovascular; sin embargo, las conclusiones se basan en un único metanálisis no replicado independientemente, y los ensayos fueron a corto plazo (semanas a meses). La calificación Moderada refleja señales tranquilizadoras en ensayos controlados pero datos a largo plazo insuficientes y estudio limitado de poblaciones de alto riesgo (p. ej., insuficiencia cardíaca avanzada).

explanation_es.evidence_base: La base de evidencia consiste enteramente en ensayos clínicos aleatorizados en humanos y un metanálisis; no se recuperaron estudios en animales para estos resultados. Los ensayos van de 2021 a 2026, con tamaños de muestra de 105 a 3417 participantes. La mayoría probó la cagrilintida en combinación con semaglutida, y la mayoría excluyó a individuos con enfermedad orgánica grave, embarazo o adolescencia. Esto significa que la evidencia es reciente y proviene de cohortes grandes en poblaciones específicas (sobrepeso, obesidad, diabetes tipo 2), pero aún no establece la eficacia o seguridad individual de la cagrilintida en poblaciones no estudiadas.
explanation_es.open_questions: Los registros proporcionados no aíslan el efecto independiente de la cagrilintida del de la semaglutida, ya que casi todos los ensayos probaron la combinación. La seguridad y eficacia a largo plazo más allá de 52 semanas están en gran medida ausentes de estos registros. Las poblaciones excluidas de los ensayos — aquellas con enfermedad renal, insuficiencia cardíaca, embarazo y niños/adolescentes — permanecen sin probar, por lo que si y cómo funciona la cagrilintida en estos grupos es desconocido según los datos mostrados aquí. Además, no aparece ninguna comparación directa con agonistas de amilina ya en uso clínico (pramlintida) en la muestra proporcionada.

appraisal_es.headline: Todos los reclamos de eficacia descansan en solo 3 ensayos clínicos aleatorizados realizados 2021–2025, todos probando cagrilintida combinada con semaglutida, lo que hace imposible aislar la contribución de cagrilintida per se o establecer su perfil de seguridad y eficacia independiente.

concerns.detail: Los tres ensayos clínicos aleatorizados para pérdida de peso (n=706, 1206, 3417) y los ensayos de diabetes explícita o implícitamente involucran cagrilintida emparejada con semaglutida. Ningún estudio aísla la eficacia de cagrilintida en monoterapia. Un escéptico no puede determinar si los efectos observados son impulsados por cagrilintida, semaglutida (ya aprobada), o su interacción. Los ensayos más grandes pueden simplemente demostrar el efecto conocido de semaglutida, con la contribución de cagrilintida indefinida.

concerns.issue: Sin metanálisis agrupado a pesar de ensayos idénticos
concerns.detail: Existen tres ensayos clínicos aleatorizados para pérdida de peso con años consecutivos (2021, 2025, 2025) y diseños similares, sin embargo el motor reporta 'sin análisis agrupado confirma que estén de acuerdo.' Para glucosa en sangre y resultados cardiovasculares, existe un solo metanálisis pero no está replicado de forma independiente. Sin síntesis formal, los reclamos de consistencia son visuales, no estadísticos; un solo resultado atípico o patrón de heterogeneidad podría invertir conclusiones sin desencadenar re-evaluación.

concerns.issue: La evidencia cardiovascular descansa en un solo estudio pequeño de QT más metanálisis observacional
concerns.detail: La calificación cardiovascular (Moderada) incluye solo un ensayo clínico aleatorizado primario (n=105, enfocado en prolongación del intervalo QT—un punto final de seguridad estrecho, no de eficacia). El metanálisis sobre efectos cardiovasculares no está verificado de forma independiente. Un solo estudio pequeño de QT no puede establecer beneficio cardiovascular en el mundo real o confirmar ausencia de daño en uso comercializado. El conjunto de datos cardiovascular más grande es el ensayo de pérdida de peso n=3417, que no fue potenciado para resultados cardiovasculares.

concerns.issue: Uso de mercado gris, no aprobado; las poblaciones de estudio pueden no representar usuarios reales
concerns.detail: La nota indica que cagrilintida es 'frecuentemente obtenida de mercado gris y no está aprobada para uso humano.' Todos los ensayos reclutaron poblaciones controladas con sobrepeso/obesidad o diabetes tipo 2 bajo supervisión médica. Los usuarios reales de mercado gris probablemente sean más mayores, tengan comorbilidades desconocidas, usen dosis desconocidas, y carezcan de monitoreo médico. La eficacia y seguridad en poblaciones de ensayos clínicos aleatorizados no puede transferirse a contextos de mercado gris no controlados.

concerns.issue: Evidencia reciente (2021–2025) sin señal de seguridad a largo plazo documentada
concerns.detail: Los cuatro años de datos recuperados son de 2021 en adelante, con la mayoría de ensayos publicados en 2025. La seguridad a largo plazo (>52 semanas) no es aparente en los títulos de estudios o tamaños de muestra. Semaglutida requirió vigilancia poscomercialización para eventos adversos raros (p. ej., pancreatitis, retinopatía); cagrilintida, siendo más nueva y siempre combinada, ha tenido exposición de mercado insuficiente para detectar daños infrecuentes.

appraisal_es.mechanism_check: Cagrilintida es un análogo agonista del receptor GLP-1; la activación de receptores GLP-1 plausiblemente suprime el apetito y mejora el control glucémico, vinculando mecanismo a pérdida de peso y resultados de azúcar en sangre. Sin embargo, porque todos los ensayos usan cagrilintida + semaglutida (ella misma un agonista GLP-1), el mecanismo que respalda el beneficio clínico reclamado no es claro: ¿está cagrilintida proporcionando un efecto aditivo o sinérgico, o simplemente confirmando que el agonismo GLP-1 funciona? El salto de 'cagrilintida + semaglutida reduce peso' a 'cagrilintida funciona' es inferencialmente grande e irresuelto.
appraisal_es.strongest_counterargument: Un escéptico argumentaría que la base de evidencia demuestra solo que semaglutida combinada con un péptido investigacional produce efectos GLP-1 esperados—no que cagrilintida tenga valor clínico independiente. La ausencia de cualquier ensayo clínico aleatorizado de cagrilintida sola, la falta de síntesis estadística agrupada, y la dependencia de un solo estudio pequeño de QT para seguridad cardiovascular significan que la evidencia es insuficiente para justificar uso no aprobado de mercado gris. Semaglutida está aprobada y estudiada; cagrilintida no; los ensayos confunden ambas y por lo tanto no respaldan recomendar cagrilintida específicamente.
appraisal_es.what_would_change_the_picture: Un ensayo aleatorizado, controlado comparando monoterapia con cagrilintida contra placebo en la misma población aislaría su efecto. Alternativamente, un registro prospectivo de usuarios de cagrilintida de mercado gris con seguimiento estandarizado y captura de eventos adversos documentaría seguridad en el mundo real e identificaría daños raros antes de que ocurran en muchos usuarios fuera de supervisión de ensayos.
